compatibility: New wire/storage version and trusted route epoch required. Existing v1 retains every record; no implicit migration.
problem: Deleting receiver evidence before sender authoritative confirmation can destroy the only recoverable first-event fact.
A sequence floor alone does not prevent reuse of a forgotten free-text delivery ID at a later sequence.
A commitment authenticates history but does not reconstruct it.

identity.delivery_id: Full lowercase hex SHA256(CBOR(["retention-delivery-id",2,context_hash,sequence])); context_hash=SHA256(CBOR(["retention-context",2,canonical_context])). Context binds deployment, route, immutable epoch, both authority namespaces, both Ed25519 key pins/kids, both TLS certificate pins and public window. Implemented in prototype/retention_wire.py; same context cannot be mutated in place.
identity.route_epoch: Trusted immutable unique incarnation; not selected or reset by an untrusted request. Bound to both authority namespaces.
identity.sequence: Candidate uint64 sequence 1..2^64-1, never wrap. Store last finalized high-water H and explicit exhaustion; next=H+1 only below maximum. Python model uses unbounded integers over finite explorations.
identity.semantic_limit: Uniqueness is per immutable route incarnation. New authorized operations can intentionally repeat application content; this is not semantic deduplication of arbitrary business requests.

state.receiver: Authoritative (route, epoch, F_R, D_F, H, clock_floor, live records F_R+1..H), with public window W; local replica must equal current authority before writes or first-event replies.
state.sender: Authoritative confirmed frontier F_S, recorded retirement frontier F_T, and retained authenticated canonical final facts through F_S. Sender evidence remains an archive.
state.ghost: Full history in retention_model.py is an assertion oracle, not bounded receiver storage.
state.commitment: Genesis=SHA256(CBOR(["retention-prefix-genesis",2,context_hash])); D_i=SHA256(CBOR(["retention-prefix-step",2,D_(i-1),canonical_fact_bytes_i])). Fact bytes contain profile/context hash, seq/derived ID, action_digest, descriptor_hash, issued_at/expires_at, outcome, event_at and envelope_hash. Challenge/request/signature bytes excluded. Implemented; complete v2 descriptor/evidence codec implemented in prototype/retention_delivery.py; L3 and both authority transactions implemented in retention_sender.py and retention_recipient.py; full refinement proof remains open.

invariants: live records equal the exact contiguous unretired history F_R+1..H
D_F commits to exactly the retired prefix
Every delivery ID is the route/epoch/sequence derived value and cannot be rebound
H and all frontiers never decrease; deletion never resets the next sequence
0 <= H-F_R <= W; admission at full window fails without changing historical facts
Retirement does not alter privacy consumption, reservations, randomness, release expiry or previous final outcomes

protocol.rule: Receiver establishes ACCEPTED or CLOSED under existing validity rules, accepts full state at its authority, commits locally, then signs its first-event receipt. Outcome/time immutable.
Sender authenticates receipt and stores its normalized final fact and contiguous F_S at sender authority before issuing any retirement authorization. Volatile receipt knowledge is insufficient.

Sender signs distinct RetireOffer domain binding exact route/epoch, both authority namespaces, base F_T, target T<=F_S and D_T. It retains supporting full facts; recipient trusts this signer to enforce durable confirmation. A signature alone does not prove persistence to an external observer.

Current local replica required. Require base==F_R, F_R<T<=H, every interval record present, recomputed D_T matches offer. Atomically advance F_R/D_F and delete exactly the prefix while preserving H/clock/route metadata. Receiver authority accepts first, local commit second, reply third.

Distinct signed RetireAck binds current challenge, complete request/offer digest, exact route/epoch/namespaces and accepted floor/root. Failed or unknown authority outcome requires current-head recovery; no unconditional second transition.

After lost reply, authenticated checkpoint read is sufficient only if sender independently matches floor<=F_S and D_F to its archived final facts. Persist F_T before preparing next base. Old offers cannot lower floor; an already applied exact target can return the current checkpoint without inventing first-event evidence.

For sequence<=F_R return authenticated RETIRED checkpoint. Never relabel as CLOSED, never fabricate first-event time, never reaccept. Exact historical recovery requires an available authenticated archive plus sufficient chain evidence.

fault_contract.before_authority: Old authoritative state remains; do not claim deletion succeeded.
fault_contract.after_authority_before_local: Freeze stale local copy and restore new authority image. The deleted prefix stays retired.
fault_contract.after_local_before_reply: Read current checkpoint with a fresh authenticated challenge and reconcile sender retained facts.
fault_contract.sender_confirm_reply_loss: Recover sender authority before deciding which target may be retired.
fault_contract.sender_or_network_permanent_failure: Window can fill and stop new work. No unconditional liveness or automatic timeout deletion.
fault_contract.both_authorities_rollback: Outside guarantee; local consistency cannot detect rollback of all trusted history.

capacity.bound: For one fixed route with bounded encodings, receiver current-state bytes <= M + W*L; M bounds permanent metadata and L bounds a maximal live record including serialization overhead.
capacity.admission_gate: Implemented in prototype/retention_recipient.py: exact schema/context metadata plus maximal frame-sized encrypted cells, actual canonical serialization; require M+W*L<=MAX_IMAGE before database creation/open or authority calls. Sufficient conservative bound, not maximal possible W. See prototype/retention_capacity_contract.json.
excluded_storage: witness commit history and old full images
capacity.current_v1: 16 MiB full-image cap and retain-all behavior remain unchanged.

information_limit.claim: If n independently varying ACCEPTED/CLOSED outcomes must be answered exactly for every historical index using retained state alone, at least n bits of distinguishable retained information are needed.
information_limit.argument: There are 2^n possible outcome histories; fewer than 2^n retained states map two histories to the same state, but the histories differ on some queried index. No deterministic exact answer can satisfy both. First-event times add information.
information_limit.qualification: This is an elementary exact-recovery counting argument, not a computational collision attack. A fixed-size cryptographic commitment may bind an archived history computationally, but does not provide archive data or availability.

induction_obligations: Base: empty route has zero frontiers, empty live set, route-bound genesis and no spent-history reset.
Finalization: current authority fence, next unique ID and available window append exactly one final fact without changing existing facts.
Confirmation: authenticated immutable receipt extends only the sender contiguous confirmed prefix.
Offer/retirement: trusted durable offer gives T<=F_S; exact matching interval/root and one atomic authority transition preserve all retained/deleted-history relations.
Checkpoint: root checked against sender retained history ensures F_T never exceeds receiver retirement or sender confirmation.
Recovery/replay: local rollback does not alter authority; fence prevents stale writes; exact authority recovery preserves all invariants.

Full implementation refinement remains a proof obligation. Both authority transactions, signed facts, uint64 storage, tested crash cuts and conservative current-image byte admission exist; this does not establish all protocol transitions, total resource bounds or complete public observations.

evidence.scope: Finite safety exploration. Drain is a fault-free macro schedule with invariant checks, not transition-by-transition liveness verification or deployed fault testing. A/C outcome validity and cryptography are abstracted.
